rationale: C20 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both orders continue or organize a President's committee, prescribe its public-facing functions, authorize subordinate advisory bodies, place direction in a presidentially designated chairman, regulate meetings, require uncompensated service, and arrange departmental administrative support. Several clauses in the child closely reproduce C20's distinctive wording and sequence, far beyond generic committee boilerplate. C15 and C18 provide weaker parallels involving citizen participation, intergovernmental cooperation, and agency support, but neither matches the child's administrative architecture and language as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There is hereby continued, subject to the provisions of this order, the President's Committee for Traffic Safety
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby continued, subject to the provisions of this order and under the name of the President's Committee on Employment of the Physically Handicapped, the now existing committee of that name
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive continuation formula used to reorganize an existing presidential committee.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Committee may establish or continue such advisory groups ... as may be necessary to assist it in carrying out its activities, [and] shall prescribe such regulations as it deems appropriate for such groups
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby established the Advisory Council ... which shall advise the President's Committee ... [and] The Chairman may from time to time prescribe such necessary rules, procedures, and policies relating to the President's Committee, the Executive Committee, and the Advisory Council
shared_material.explanation: Both establish subordinate advisory machinery and authorize rules governing the committee and its auxiliary bodies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Chairman of the Committee shall be designated by the President and shall direct the work of the Committee. The Chairman may designate a Vice Chairman to serve as Chairman in his absence. The Chairman may from time to time prescribe such necessary rules, procedures, and policies ... as are not inconsistent with law or with the provisions of this order.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Chairman of the President's Committee shall on behalf of the President direct the Committee and its functions. ... the Chairman ... may from time to time designate a Vice Chairman ... in the absence of the Chairman ... The Chairman may from time to time prescribe such necessary rules, procedures, and policies ... as are not inconsistent with law or with the provisions of this order.
shared_material.explanation: This is an unusually close verbal and functional match in a multi-clause chairman provision.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Committee shall meet annually, and at such other times and places as the Chairman may deem necessary. Members of the Committee shall serve without compensation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The President's Committee ... shall each meet on the call of the Chairman ... The Chairman shall call at least one meeting ... during each calendar year. ... All members ... shall serve without compensation.
shared_material.explanation: Parallel sequence governing chairman-called meetings, a minimum annual meeting, and uncompensated membership.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of Commerce may make available to the Committee ... such office space, staff, equipment, supplies, and services as may be necessary for the operations of the Committee.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Department of Labor is requested to make available to the President's Committee necessary office space and to furnish the Committee ... necessary equipment, supplies, and services.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical departmental-support clause, adapted from Labor to Commerce and adding the child's statutory limitation.
